A 25-year-old woman, gravida 2 para 2, visits her primary care physician for follow-up two weeks after
delivering a 9.5 lb (4.3 kg) male infant via vaginal delivery. The delivery was complicated by a vaginal
laceration that required extensive suturing. Immediately after placental delivery, she experienced
intense shaking and chills that resolved within an hour. Since then, she has felt well but reports six
days of malodorous, tan-colored vaginal discharge. She has a history of vaginal candidiasis and is
concerned it may have recurred. Her temperature is 97.2°F (37.1°C), blood pressure is 102/76 mmHg,

pulse is 86/min, respirations are 18/min, and BMI is 33 kg/m^2. On speculum examination, a 1.5 cm
dark red, velvety lesion is observed on the posterior vaginal wall along with tan discharge. The
discharge has a pH of 6.4. What is the most likely diagnosis? Answer Choices: (A) Retained products
of conception (B) Vaginal hematoma (C) Vaginal neoplasm (D) Pelvic inflammatory disease (E)
Urethrovaginal fistula (F) Rectovaginal fistula (G) Vaginal candidiasis (H) Bacterial vaginosis (I)
Granuloma formation due to sutures (J) Endometritis
 A. Urethrovaginal fistula
B. Bacterial vaginosis
C. Endometritis
D. Granuloma formation due to sutures
E. Retained products of conception
F. Pelvic inflammatory disease
G. Vaginal neoplasm
H. Rectovaginal fistula
I. Vaginal candidiasis
J. Vaginal hematoma
